problem: 1 Where do I start: give me the steps

layers.text: Parents say they don't know who/what/when/how and ask for a step list.
A first recruiting video, camp invite, or a peer committing makes the family realize the process exists; often 8th-10th grade.
layers.source: v3/W7-segments/raw/ytc_ogjICDcgCro.json (class-of-2030 asks when to email); v3/W6-problems/PROBLEMS.md #5

layers.text: No neutral owner of the process: HS coach is not responsible, the NCAA publishes rules not plans, services sell rather than teach.
Ask in TikTok comments, 'DM me', join FB groups, read blogs.
Answers are pitches or lead magnets; big FB groups ban school-specific questions; advice conflicts.
Time and missed windows (e.g. D1/D2 contact opens Jun 15 / Sep 1 after sophomore yr); risk of paying a service out of panic.
Athlete loses months of outreach; parent carries the stress; spouses disagree on spend.
'Tell me, for my kid's grade and sport, the 3 things to do this month.'
Free 'Start here by grade + sport' page that outputs a dated monthly checklist from the rule calendar, then routes to the Sport Pack.
Parent can name this month's 3 tasks and the next contact date; checklist items ticked; first coach email sent within 14 days.

problem: 2 Is it too late? Junior/senior with nothing

layers.text: 'My kid is a senior/junior and we have nothing. Is it too late?'
Summer before senior year: teammates commit, D2 boards look full, a dream school goes silent.
Started outreach late and aimed too high; never assessed realistic level.
Mass-email, buy a service, post on X, attend late camps.
Wrong targets (P4/D1 boards filled by August), unanswered emails, no follow-up plan.
Eligibility of the window: roster spots filled; possible JUCO detour; money on panic services.
Athlete's confidence; club coaches; target coaches still filling the roster for next year.
'Find the programs still filling our class and get us in front of them before signing day.'
Senior-year sprint playbook: level reset to D2/D3/NAIA/JUCO, 30-school list, 4-touch follow-up cadence, 'we'll be in your area' visit email, JUCO/post-grad fallback.
A coach reply or visit invite within 30 days; a roster spot or JUCO plan in hand by graduation.

problem: 3 Is NCSA/a recruiting service worth it, and how do I cancel?

layers.text: Regret after paying; aggressive calls; can't cancel; 'is it worth it?'
Unsolicited call/text from a service after a free profile or camp, often to a young athlete.
Parents don't know what is free (NCAA rules, email, X) and fear their kid is invisible without paying.
Sign up, sometimes at a 'discount'; ask groups.
Coaches dislike agency contact; services did nothing families couldn't do; prices hidden till end of call; refund refused under hardship.
Money: parents report up to ~$4K plus monthly fees; a contract during income loss.
Athlete (coaches ignore service emails); a minority report real offers, so families split.
'Get the organization and timeline a service gives, without the price or the sales pressure.'
Honest 'service vs DIY' comparison + cancel guide + the same timeline/tracker for a fixed low price.
Family cancels or never signs; saves the fee; still sends weekly outreach from the tracker.

problem: 4 What do I say to a coach, and on which channel?

layers.text: 'What do I actually write, and email vs X DM vs questionnaire?'
First outreach push, or weeks of silence after the first emails.
Emails written by parents, no grad year in subject, no film link, sent before contact dates.
Random templates, mass DMs, creators' dead links.
Coaches skim and delete; D1/D2 can't reply before Jun 15/Sep 1 dates; silence read as rejection.
Time; a burned first impression with a target program.
Athlete must own it (coaches spot parent-written mail); target coaches flooded.
'Get a reply from the coaches who fit us.'
Sport-specific email/DM scripts written in the athlete's voice + follow-up cadence tied to the contact calendar.
Reply rate per 10 emails sent; first coach reply.

problem: 5 When can coaches contact us, and when should we start?

layers.text: 'When can coaches contact us, and when should we start?'
Younger sibling or 8th-9th grader gets a service call; peers talk about offers.
Rules differ by division and sport and change; most sources don't cite the bylaw.
Ask creators; follow services' 'start freshman year' advice.
Conflicting advice; emailing D1 coaches early gets no reply by rule.
Wasted early spend; anxiety; or missed contact-opening dates.
Coaches bound by rules; athlete confused by silence.
'Know exactly what's allowed now and what date to act next.'
Bylaw-cited rule calendar by sport/division with date reminders.
Parent acts on the opening date (e.g. Jun 15 after soph year) instead of guessing.

problem: 6 How do I register with the NCAA / get the ID, and what does it cost?

layers.text: 'How do I get the NCAA ID? What does it cost?'
A coach asks for the ID, or an official visit is scheduled.
Confusion among NCAA ID, Eligibility Center Certification vs Profile account, fee, and NCSA.
Ask creators and groups.
Mixed timing advice ('register sophomore year' vs 'don't apply yet').
Eligibility: no Certification account and transcripts means no D1/D2 official visit.
HS counselor (transcripts), college compliance, athlete.
'Make sure nothing on paper blocks my kid.'
Step-by-step Eligibility Center + NAIA registration walkthrough with fee and deadline.
Account created, transcripts sent, official visit not blocked.
